items.definition:
determine the order for dealing with (a series of tasks or projects) according to their relative importance
You need to prioritise your tasks to meet the deadline.

to flow or leak slowly through porous material or small holes
Water began to seep through the cracks in the ceiling.

overcome
She managed to surmount the many obstacles in her path.

to become unsteady or indecisive
His voice began to waver as he delivered the emotional speech.

to assess the value or quality of
The jeweler was asked to appraise the diamond.

to enchant; to charm
The magician seemed to bewitch the audience with his tricks.

To be filled with a feeling of love for.
He was completely enamored with her beauty.

To struggle clumsily or helplessly.
The company began to flounder after losing its main client.

to start or restart something quickly or with renewed energy
We need to kickstart the project to meet the deadline.

treat with an apparent kindness that betrays a feeling of superiority; or, support (a store, restaurant, etc.) regularly.
Please don't patronize me; I understand perfectly well.

to respond to a gesture or action by making a corresponding one
She was quick to reciprocate his kindness.

to enjoy or appreciate something fully
She savoured every bite of the delicious meal.

to speak to someone or about something in a scornfully derisive or mocking way
He scoffed at the idea of working for free.

to calm or make someone sleep by administering a sedative drug
The vet had to sedate the anxious dog before the examination.

to wriggle, to fidget
The child began to squirm in his seat during the long lecture.

to send off to a destination or for a purpose
The goods were despatched yesterday and should arrive tomorrow.

to suggest or hint in an indirect and unpleasant way
Are you trying to insinuate that I'm lying?

To form a wrong opinion or conclusion about.
I'm afraid I misjudged the situation completely.

to distribute something differently or again
The government plans to redistribute wealth more evenly.

to sit or stand with one leg on either side of something
He had to straddle the fence to get over it.

to dance in a sexually provocative manner
The dancer began to twerk to the beat of the music.

to release from chains
The zookeeper had to unchain the gate to enter the enclosure.

to perform baptism
The priest will baptise the baby next Sunday.

to cry or shout loudly
The baby started to bawl when it woke up.

to overturn (a boat)
The strong winds caused the small boat to capsize.

reduce or underestimate the worth of
The company's shares began to devalue rapidly.

leave the main subject temporarily in speech or writing
Let's try not to digress too much from the main topic.

understand and share the feelings of another
It's important to empathize with others' struggles.

to become infected; to worsen over time
The wound began to fester after a few days.

to be a warning or indication of a future event
The dark clouds foreshadowed the coming storm.

to bring under state control
The government decided to nationalize the failing bank.

to get rid of something or someone
They needed to offload the excess inventory before the new stock arrived.

to estimate something to be larger or better than it really is
He overestimated his ability to finish the project on time.

to put too great a load on
Be careful not to overload the washing machine.

to feed a baby or young animal from the breast or teat
The mother cat began to suckle her kittens.

to bite at or nibble something persistently
The dog loved to gnaw on its bone.

To annoy or irritate.
His constant complaining began to irk her.

live longer than
She hopes to outlive her grandmother, who is 95.

to predict what will happen
The old woman claimed she could prophesy the future.

to move around stealthily
A tiger was seen prowling in the tall grass.

to search a place thoroughly, often causing disorder or damage
The burglars ransacked the house looking for valuables.

burn slowly without flame
The campfire continued to smolder long after the flames died down.

form or join a labor union
The workers decided to unionize to demand better wages.

to gradually withdraw from something
It's time to wean the baby off milk and onto solid foods.

to squeeze and twist to extract liquid
She had to wring out the wet towel before hanging it to dry.

to spoil the surface or appearance of (something) with writing or drawings
Vandals defaced the statue with graffiti.

Choose carefully or personally.
She was handpicked for the leadership role.

perform less well than expected
The company's stock continued to underperform the market.

to cause or accelerate (a reaction) by acting as a catalyst
Enzymes catalyze biochemical reactions in the body.

to take part in an activity in a casual or superficial way
She likes to dabble in painting, but she's not a serious artist.

to stand or wait around idly or without apparent purpose
Teenagers often loiter outside the convenience store.

to calm or soothe
The mother tried to pacify the crying baby.

to fold into pleats
She carefully pleated the fabric for the skirt.

to reject or refuse abruptly
Her offer of help was met with a sharp rebuff.

to recover from illness or exertion
He needed time to recuperate after the surgery.

to make or become sick or disgusted
The sight of the cruelty made her sicken.

to steal
He was caught trying to thieve from the shop.

reverse one's previous statement or position; return by the same route
He had to backtrack on his promise after realizing his mistake.

to defeat or outdo
He managed to best his opponent in the final round.

to fry food lightly and then stew it slowly in a closed container
The chef decided to braise the short ribs for several hours.

a three-beat gait of a horse, slower than a gallop
The horse broke into a gentle canter across the field.

to form a foam or froth
He lathered the soap in his hands before washing.

to blend or combine
The flavors of the ingredients meld perfectly in this dish.

to change the focus or direction of attention
After the break, we need to refocus on our main goals.
